2608.01995.title: Long-Horizon Autonomous Architecture Research with a Language-Model Agent: A Behavioural Case Study
2608.01995.paper_summary: We study what happens when a single general-purpose large language model acts as the sole researcher on a long-horizon neural architecture design problem. The agent receives a scientific question, an initial hypothesis and motivation, a compute budget, and research affordances (source and experiment management, experiment tracking, literature access, and persistent memory), then autonomously proposes, implements, evaluates, and records experiments over an extended period. The study comprises three phases, separated by human-declared transitions, that progressively expand the agent's tool surface or problem scale. Across approximately 100 sequential experiments, the agent improves a non-standard Vision Transformer from a weak baseline to a stronger, efficient model on small benchmarks and a usable but sub-SOTA model on ImageNet-1K, while producing a dense behavioural trace. We report four findings.(i)Productivity exhibits a clear phase structure: rapid early gains, a multi-dozen-hypothesis saturation wall, and recovery, with recovery triggered by expanding the action surface rather than changing the underlying model.(ii)A single early hypothesis contributes more to accuracy gain, with later improvements long-tailed.(iii)The preference for greedy, incremental hypotheses is largely workflow-induced: a commit-or-discard evaluation rule is isomorphic to greedy hill-climbing; the remainder reflects risk aversion after bold failures and anchoring on familiar literature. (iv)The agent independently rediscovers established results and, in the unfamiliar regime of pure channel attention, overturns a standard design choice. We conclude that workflow design was at least as influential as agent capability in this study and propose diversified search, budgeted moonshot hypotheses, explicit forks, and regime-aware re-validation as testable directions for future autonomous research.
2608.01995.paper_summary_zh: 我們研究當一個通用的大型語言模型作為長期神經架構設計問題的唯一研究者時會發生什麼。該代理接收一個科學問題、一個初步假設和動機、一個計算預算，以及研究資源（來源和實驗管理、實驗跟踪、文獻訪問和持久記憶），然後自主提出、實施、評估和記錄實驗，持續一段時間。這項研究包括三個階段，通過人類宣告的過渡來分隔，逐步擴展代理的工具範圍或問題規模。在大約100個連續實驗中，該代理將一個非標準的視覺Transformer從一個較弱的基準提升到一個更強大、有效的模型，在小型基準上表現良好，而在ImageNet-1K上則是一個可用但低於SOTA的模型，同時產生密集的行為痕跡。我們報告了四個發現。(i)生產力顯示出明顯的階段結構：早期迅速增長、多十個假設的飽和牆和恢復，恢復是由擴展行動範圍而非改變基礎模型觸發的。(ii)單一的早期假設對準確度的提升貢獻更大，後期的改進呈長尾分佈。(iii)對貪婪、增量假設的偏好在很大程度上是由工作流程引起的：一個承諾或放棄的評估規則與貪婪的爬坡相同；其餘反映了在大膽失敗後的風險厭惡和對熟悉文獻的依賴。(iv)該代理獨立重新發現了既有結果，並在純通道注意力的陌生範疇中推翻了一個標準設計選擇。我們得出結論，工作流程設計在這項研究中的影響力至少與代理能力同等，並提出多樣化搜索、預算月球射擊假設、明確的分叉和考慮範疇的重新驗證作為未來自主研究的可測試方向。
2608.01995.author: Aon Safdar et.al.
